flashpoints.title: Control without ownership
flashpoints.mechanism: Dual-class shares give a founder the vote while the public supplies the capital.
flashpoints.outcome: Zuckerberg holds about 61% of Meta's votes on about 13% of the shares; Page and Brin hold 52.7% of Alphabet's votes; Musk holds more than 82% of SpaceX's.

flashpoints.title: OpenAI's recapitalisation
flashpoints.advantage: capital and compute traded for a stake
flashpoints.mechanism: The nonprofit kept control while Microsoft, the compute supplier, converted its funding into a 27% stake.
flashpoints.outcome: Foundation 26%, Microsoft about 27%, investors and employees 47%.

flashpoints.title: The supplier owns its customers
flashpoints.advantage: a high share price turned into equity in customers
flashpoints.mechanism: NVIDIA invests in the labs and neoclouds that buy its GPUs, so demand and ownership rise together.
flashpoints.outcome: NVIDIA put $30bn into OpenAI, owns 10.29% of CoreWeave and a stake in Intel now worth more than $25bn.

flashpoints.title: Two clouds, one lab
flashpoints.mechanism: Anthropic took money from both rivals but capped their stakes and issues them non-voting shares.

notes: Verified here: 13F top-holder rows from Yahoo Finance (30 Jun 2026) for the giants; founders' and insiders' stakes from Revenue Memo's ownership explainers (secondary, citing proxies) and Reuters; OpenAI's recapitalisation (TechCrunch, 28 Oct 2025), its 2026 round (Yahoo/Reuters-style report), Anthropic's caps (S-1 as summarised by Leverage Shares), Series G/H leads; the Fed's Z.1 (L.224) for household, foreign and fund equity holdings (Q3 2025, the latest in the 9 Jan 2026 release; dated2026 false). Unverified, in notes only: SEC pages (DEF 14A, 14C, Berkshire, Meta) returned 403 to the script, so Zuckerberg's 60.6% (Nov 2026 information statement), Page 27.4% and Brin 25.3% of Alphabet's votes, Huang's 3.58% (proxy of 23 Mar 2026), Ellison's 38% (2026 proxy; 413m pledged shares) and Musk's 48.4% of SpaceX in a regulatory filing come from search summaries only. SoftBank's 87% of Arm (March 2025) and NBIM's year-end 2025 stakes (NVIDIA 1.26%, Microsoft 1.35% to 1.26%) were not fetchable; PIF, QIA, ADIA and Mubadala stakes in the US giants do not appear in the 13F top-ten lists. Yahoo splits Vanguard into Capital Management and Portfolio Management; each row cited is one entity, so Vanguard's total is higher (for example Apple: 6.60% plus 2.30%). AMD rows failed the gate and were removed.
